scores.evidence: Same-engine CDC is far more reliable, and an engine change on top of a migration compounds risk.
scores.rationale: Technical claims about CDC, read-your-writes, write-hold semantics, singleton guards, SELECT-only read enforcement and NIST 800-88 are all accurate, and it honestly states real limits (CDC LOB/computed-column gaps, <30s write pause).

scores.evidence: What "without downtime" means here: no user-visible outage. The single write cutover still pauses writes for a few seconds (target under 30 s)
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves the zero-downtime ambiguity explicitly and honestly, is buildable with ordinary tooling, and defers out-of-scope work with reasons (§7).

scores.evidence: CP, one writer. Exactly one database is authoritative at any moment. No dual-writes, no multi-master.
scores.rationale: The single-writer invariant, proxy routing control point, write-authority flag and singleton guard are honored consistently across every phase with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: 7 days of outbound dry-run with a 100% match against on-prem messages.
scores.rationale: Shadow diffing, message-level dry-runs, 2× peak load tests, three cutover rehearsals plus a rollback rehearsal, and post-cutover double-booking detection validate the riskiest decisions early and continue in production.

scores.evidence: Assumptions to confirm before Phase 0: Vendor product? If the system is a vendor product... the vendor's hosting program decides the migration path
scores.rationale: Key assumptions are explicit with confirmation steps, numbers are labeled targets to confirm (RTO/RPO), and every decision carries a stated revisit trigger describing what changes if it is wrong.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: Split-brain writes... double-booked OR or clinic slots... A close second is outbound feeds firing twice
scores.rationale: Covers the domain's hardest failures — split-brain, duplicate SIU/SMS sends, missed consumers, stale reads, CDC lag, corruption — each with concrete detection (diff dashboards, double-booking detector) and recovery (DLQs, reverse CDC, rollback triggers).

scores.evidence: Cutover runbook as code... At least 3 full rehearsals and at least 1 full rollback rehearsal... Time each one.
scores.rationale: IaC-only deployment, domain-meaningful signals (CDC lag, shadow-diff rate, ACK alarms, stale-read counter), rehearsed rollback, change freeze, war-room and hypercare make this operable by a realistic hospital IT team.

scores.evidence: Revisit after migration only if licensing cost is over budget. That becomes its own project.
scores.rationale: Licensing, build-vs-buy trade-offs and a cost dashboard are mentioned, but the dominant costs — months of dual-running both environments, private circuits, managed DB, CDC tooling and engineering time — are never estimated or analyzed.

scores.evidence: On-prem stays a hot standby after cutover, fed by reverse CDC (cloud → on-prem), for 30–90 days.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (engine change, re-architecture, multi-master) are explicitly deferred or forbidden, every decision has a revisit trigger, and the rollback path is kept alive and rehearsed until cloud DR is proven.

scores.evidence: Replatform. Same app code on cloud VMs or containers... No refactoring during the move.
scores.rationale: Keeps the monolith and same DB engine, buys commodity tooling, defers all speculative work (services, autoscaling, AI, multi-region), and every added component — proxy indirection, reconciliation, rehearsals — is justified by patient-safety risk.

scores.evidence: Phases (ordered by dependency; within a phase, widest impact first)
scores.rationale: Concrete ordered tasks with stated dependency reasoning, measurable exit checks per phase (14 days lag p99 <5s, 100% message match), and explicit adaptation triggers mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: BAA signed; landing-zone policy guardrails; private endpoints only; CMK encryption; TLS 1.2+; AD federation; read-only DB login
list every reader and writer: ADT inbound, SIU outbound, reminder/IVR vendor, billing, reporting/BI, and ODBC links from Access or Excel
hourly row counts plus per-table checksums, and a nightly full-hash comparison of the appointment and slot tables
Exactly one database is authoritative at any moment. No dual-writes, no multi-master. The cloud copy is read-only until the cutover.
Reverse CDC (cloud → on-prem), built and verified in staging. This is the rollback mechanism.
Redundant private link: ExpressRoute or Direct Connect, plus a backup IPsec VPN
The DR failover test meets RTO ≤ 1 h and RPO ≤ 5 min (targets to confirm with clinical ops).
Federate to the existing hospital AD (Entra ID / SAML). No new user store.
Load-test the cloud at 2× the observed peak, for example the Monday 08:00 booking surge.
Choose a low-volume window (e.g. Sunday 02:00, avoiding month-end and holidays). Put downtime procedures and print-ready schedules on standby.
Decommission with NIST 800-88 media sanitization certificates.

traps.evidence: Ramp read routing through the proxy: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%, department by department, with automated canary analysis

Keep the monolith as-is... Re-architecting is deferred (§7). Never during the migration.

note: An exemplary migration plan — single-writer discipline, rehearsed rollback, interface dry-runs and provisional targets throughout — weakened only by thin cost analysis and no explicit MFA/break-glass access definition.
